summary: The article argues that falling costs and easier-to-use IoT devices are letting Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) close the supply chain gap with larger corporations. It credits SME agility, simpler legacy systems and real-time data for the gains, while naming skills shortages and cybersecurity as the main challenges. Industry figures are quoted on cost, lead-time reduction, integration, and security.
one_line: IoT is becoming affordable and usable for SMEs, giving them agility and real-time visibility in supply chains while skills and security remain challenges.
key_facts: As of September 2023, smaller businesses are rapidly catching up with larger corporations in supply chain technology thanks to the democratization of IoT.
Joe Harper, CEO of EfficientFlow, a supply chain consultancy specializing in IoT integration, said SMEs are now leveraging IoT to compete with larger corporations 'at a level playing field.'
IoT enables SMEs to track products in real time, perform predictive maintenance on machinery, and manage inventory better.
On October 15, 2023, Linda Gonzales, COO of TechSolutions, said a small manufacturer client reduced lead time by 30% using IoT-driven real-time monitoring.
On November 3, 2023, Brian Tan, head of IoT start-up ConnectIoT, said IoT devices have fallen in price due to mass production and technological advances.
ConnectIoT offers modular and scalable IoT solutions for SMEs, letting them start with basic applications and scale up while avoiding large upfront investments.
On December 1, 2023, IT consultant Jane Matthews said at a supply chain workshop that 'the lack of in-house IT expertise is a considerable challenge for SMEs.'
SMEs can address skill gaps by working with third-party experts and vendors offering end-to-end IoT solutions.
SMEs often have less complex, more modern systems, which can make integrating IoT easier than for larger corporations with rigid legacy systems.
Ray Parker, CTO of SynchroChain, has observed IoT vendors creating plug-and-play solutions for SMEs' integration needs.
IoT lets SMEs monitor inventory levels, condition of goods, transportation and delivery statuses, and environmental conditions during shipping, which helps with perishables and sensitive commodities.
Cybersecurity expert Nathan O’Reilly spoke at a seminar on January 12, 2024, and advised that 'SMEs must choose IoT partners who value security as much as they do.'
IoT platforms increasingly include built-in security features, reducing risk for smaller businesses.
